name: Islo

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go (Team list rates)
modes.note: CPU billed per allocated core while running; RAM per provisioned GB; custom integer vcpus/memory_mb/disk_gb with no published limits. Idle-but-running bills at full rate until pause_after_idle fires. Paused/stopped: $0 compute. Basis verified 2026-09-28: CPU "$0.07/CPU-hour" billed "per core while the env runs"; memory "per GB you provision" (https://islo.dev/pricing). pause_after_idle: "Pause after this many seconds without activity (no exec, file I/O, port traffic, etc.)" (https://docs.islo.dev/concepts/sandbox-lifecycle.md).

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Signup credits, no card; amount unpublished. 5-concurrent cap per launch press coverage (The New Stack), not on islo.dev.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: Pay-as-you-go at list rates; no seat licenses. 50 concurrent running sandboxes per press coverage; paused sandboxes don't count.

plans.name: AWS Marketplace Team Starter
plans.note: $50/month contract = $50 monthly credits ('294 hours compute for most customers'), no refunds; overage handling and rollover unspecified in listing. Concurrency 50 assumed = Team plan ('Team Starter Package'); was null, which let the engine bypass the Team 50-concurrent cap via this plan (verifier 2026-09-28).

plans.name: Enterprise / BYOC
plans.note: Custom packages; FAQ: 'You still pay for compute time. BYOC deployment terms may vary.'

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.

knobs.label: Idle tail before pause_after_idle (x session hours)
knobs.why: Idle-but-running sandboxes bill full allocated CPU/RAM until the pause_after_idle lifecycle timer fires; without a policy they bill until deleted, and the policy is immutable after creation. Paused = $0 compute. Factor = (session + idle timer) / session.

caveats: Billing granularity and minimum per start unpublished ('billed per hour' / 'per vCPU-hour'); per-second metering not confirmed.
Whether disk is billed while paused/stopped is unresolved: FAQ says 'No charge when stopped' but storage is a listed $0.0007/GB-h meter.
Named snapshot storage price unpublished (snapshot_gib_month null); if billed at the disk rate it would be $0.511/GB-month.
Disk billed per provisioned GB with no stated free allowance; included_disk_gib=0 reflects that, and the engine should add W.disk x $0.0007/GB-h while running.
Free (5 concurrent) / Team (50 concurrent) / Enterprise tiers come from launch press coverage (The New Stack, May 2026), not an Islo page.
Signup credit amount unpublished; Harbor users get $250 one-time via promo code HARBOR250 (not modeled in free.one_time_credit).
Egress, IPv4 and region pricing unpublished; no public IPv4 product (HTTPS shares + CLI tunnel only).
Gateway inference (Islo-managed LLMs) draws from the same credits at unpublished token rates.
Lifecycle policy (pause_after_idle etc.) is immutable after creation; sandboxes without it bill at full rate while idle.
Heavy paused sandboxes can take 5-7 min to become resumable (third-party report).
No benchmark data for islo in benchmarks.json.

Official RL page cost example bills 10-minute tasks pro rata (500 tasks x ~10 min at 4 vCPU / 1 GB / ~2 GB disk = $26.78, ~$0.054/task), so metering is at least sub-hour in practice. Exact granularity and per-start minimum are still unpublished; the engine should not assume hourly rounding.

Official pages show 300 concurrent Harbor rollouts ('--n-concurrent 300', 'hundreds of concurrent rollouts'), well above the press-reported 50-concurrent Team cap. The cap is probably raisable, but it is still not published on any Islo page.

fleet.verification: Official pricing says signup credits with no card; further screening not published.
fleet.tiers: Launch coverage reports Free 5, Team 50, Enterprise custom; current official pricing does not republish numeric tier limits.
fleet.notes: Third-party-reported concurrency: The New Stack launch article, not independently confirmed by current official quota docs. Thus 10/50 via reported Team path only; 300/1,000 custom unverified. Lifecycle docs confirm paused sandboxes do not count toward running quota. Launch article also mentions private beta; confirm current admission. Current self-serve tier activation/increase mechanism is not independently verified, so raise remains null.

snapshot_auto.quote: When a timer fires, the platform **pauses** the VM: state is snapshotted, compute is released, and the sandbox no longer counts against running-sandbox quotas. Paused sandboxes keep their filesystem and can be resumed.
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in lifecycle policy set at creation (immutable): pause_after_idle (no exec/file I/O/port traffic) and/or pause_after (active-runtime cap); auto_resume=on_activity resumes transparently on the next exec/file/webhook. Memory included: 'files, processes, and in-memory state are restored on resume' (https://docs.islo.dev/cli/sandbox-commands.md, islo pause). Without a policy nothing pauses automatically.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshots let you capture the complete state of a running sandbox and restore it later.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Named snapshots (islo snapshot save / POST snapshots) are filesystem-only ('The snapshot captures the entire filesystem state'), from a running sandbox; restore always creates a NEW sandbox ('Restoring from a snapshot creates a new sandbox'), so they work as templates/forks (many sandboxes from one snapshot). Memory-including state is only via pause/resume of the same sandbox (manual islo pause or API).

harness_api.quote: Harness and model live on the `run_agent` step, never in `line.toml`.
harness_api.note: Jobs / factory lines (API + CLI) run a first-party run_agent step with harness codex, claude, cursor or opencode (+ 'custom' exec) and a prompt; runs expose events (islo factory line-run events), follow-ups and mid-stage agent turns (line-run follow-up / agent-turn / ask), steer/stop/retry. Harness list from Islo's own skills repo (harness-models-knowledge.md: '`harness` must be a literal (`codex`, `claude`, `cursor`, or `opencode`)'). Also CLI: 'islo use --agent claude --task "..."' starts Claude Code/Cursor/Codex in a persistent background session and resumes Claude Code sessions on reconnect (https://docs.islo.dev/cli/agent-integration.md).

egress_allowlist.quote: A gateway profile is a network policy plus an ordered set of rules — each rule matches outbound traffic by host (and optionally path/method) and decides whether to allow it, deny it, or inject credentials before forwarding.
egress_allowlist.note: Gateway profile per sandbox: --default-action allow|deny (default-deny possible), host globs ('*.anthropic.com'), --internet-access true/false (also internet_enabled on create-sandbox). Host-based; no IP/CIDR rules documented. Rules changed after creation need sandbox recreate/reconnect.

egress_http_rules.quote: Restrict to one or more HTTP methods (`GET`, `POST`, …)
egress_http_rules.note: Per-rule path pattern, HTTP methods, rate limit (rpm), and request/response content filters (regex, content-type, size-limit, and an LLM 'judge' filter with Anthropic/OpenAI model per the API reference create-gateway-rule).

ingress_rules.quote: Islo lets you create shareable URLs for HTTP services running inside your sandbox.
ingress_rules.note: Ports are not public by default: you choose a port to share (islo share <sandbox> [port]) with a TTL (default 24h, e.g. 30m-7d) and revoke with islo unshare; shares are public HTTPS URLs (API: 'Create a temporary public share for a sandbox port'), no auth/IP allowlist on the share itself. Non-HTTP access via authenticated islo port-forward tunnel. Incoming webhooks authenticate (HMAC/bearer/basic) before delivering to a port.

guest_firewall.note: Each sandbox is 'a microVM with its own kernel' (https://islo.dev/sandboxes) with root/sudo (setup scripts use sudo apt-get; Docker inside supported), so iptables/nftables inside should work. Not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Credentials never reach the sandbox process — authentication happens at the host/network layer.
secret_proxy.note: Gateway rules inject a stored provider key as bearer/basic/custom header for any host; integrations cover GitHub, Slack, Anthropic/OpenAI/Cursor and tenant custom services (API key or OAuth). Sandboxes see phantom placeholder env vars (values starting 'islo_p') replaced on egress (islo-labs/skills gateway-integrations.md). AWS: IAM role assumed via STS through the gateway, no long-lived keys in the sandbox (https://docs.islo.dev/integrations/aws.md). Git over HTTPS to GitHub covered; SSH/database protocols not documented. Islo inference (gateway.islo.dev) additionally provides platform-owned model credentials.

volume_attach.note: Create-sandbox schema has disk_gb but no volume/mount fields; no volume concept anywhere in the docs index. Persistence is via pause/resume and snapshots. Users can self-mount S3 with mount-s3 via the AWS cloud-role integration (third-party FUSE, not a first-party volume).

volume_shared.note: No shared volume/filesystem product. Sharing between sandboxes is only via snapshots (copy) or a user-mounted S3 bucket (mount-s3 over the AWS integration, read-write per IAM policy). 'Knowledge' is a versioned document store API, not a filesystem.
